To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) breast cancer patients’ experiences with the disease were not only physical and medical but also psychological; 2) the psychological experiences were not only negative and painful but also positive and enriching; 3) the psychological experiences of breast cancer patients were not only individual but also social; 4) the social psychological experiences were not negative and painful but positive and enriching.
breast cancer patients who had a history of sexual abuse and who were diagnosed at an early stage of breast cancer, reported a higher number of symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
the most frequently mentioned coping strategy was “positive attitude”, followed by “acceptance” and “social support”.
